\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{आपदा} (āpdā)}{आपदा (āpdā)}]{\hi{आपदा} (āpdā) — a disaster; a calamity}

\label{lesson:HI-C302-apda}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for to melt, then the Hindi for a blister.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{आपदा}}
\textbf{\hi{आपदा}} — \emph{āpdā} — \textquotedblleft{}a disaster; a calamity\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{पिछले} \hi{साल} \hi{गाँव} \hi{में} \hi{बाढ़} \hi{की} \hi{बड़ी} \hi{आपदा} \hi{आई।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pichle sāl gā̃v meṁ bāṛh kī baṛī āpdā āī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Last year a great flood disaster struck the village.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
is Sanskrit \emph{āpad}, \textquotedblleft{}misfortune, distress\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), with the feminine ending Hindi gives it. It is the word of the news and of government: a flood, a storm or an earthquake is an \textbf{\hi{आपदा}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āpdā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āpdā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pichle sāl gā̃v meṁ bāṛh kī baṛī āpdā āī.} — Last year a great flood disaster struck the village.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for to melt, then the Hindi for a blister, then say \emph{āpdā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{आपदा} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A disaster; a calamity\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{चेतावनी} (cetāvnī)}{चेतावनी (cetāvnī)}]{\hi{चेतावनी} (cetāvnī) — a warning}

\label{lesson:HI-C302-cetavni}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a blister, then the Hindi for a disaster.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{चेतावनी}}
\textbf{\hi{चेतावनी}} — \emph{cetāvnī} — \textquotedblleft{}a warning\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{चेतावनी} \hi{के} \hi{बाद} \hi{लोगों} \hi{को} \hi{गाँव} \hi{छोड़ना} \hi{पड़ा।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{cetāvnī ke bād logoṁ ko gā̃v choṛnā paṛā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
After the warning people had to leave the village.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{चेतावनी}} (\emph{cetāvnī}) is built on \emph{cetānā}, to make someone aware, probably from the Sanskrit family of \emph{cetana}, \textquotedblleft{}awareness\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams). It is feminine: \textbf{\hi{चेतावनी} \hi{दी}}, gave a warning.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cetāvnī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cetāvnī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cetāvnī ke bād logoṁ ko gā̃v choṛnā paṛā.} — After the warning people had to leave the village.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for a blister, then the Hindi for a disaster, then say \emph{cetāvnī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{चेतावनी} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A warning\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{ऐलान} (ailān)}{ऐलान (ailān)}]{\hi{ऐलान} (ailān) — an announcement}

\label{lesson:HI-C302-ailan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a disaster, then the Hindi for a warning.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{ऐलान}}
\textbf{\hi{ऐलान}} — \emph{ailān} — \textquotedblleft{}an announcement\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{गाँव} \hi{के} \hi{मंदिर} \hi{से} \hi{ऐलान} \hi{हुआ} \hi{कि} \hi{नदी} \hi{में} \hi{पानी} \hi{ऊपर} \hi{आ} \hi{रहा} \hi{है।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{gā̃v ke mandir se ailān huā ki nadī meṁ pānī ūpar ā rahā hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
An announcement came from the village temple that the river was rising.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{ऐलान}} (\emph{ailān}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{iʿlān}, \textquotedblleft{}a making known\textquotedblright{}. It begins with the letter \textbf{\hi{ऐ}}, the vowel of \textbf{\hi{ऐसा}}. \textbf{\hi{ऐलान} \hi{करना}} is to announce.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ailān}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ailān}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gā̃v ke mandir se ailān huā ki nadī meṁ pānī ūpar ā rahā hai.} — An announcement came from the village temple that the river was rising.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for a disaster, then the Hindi for a warning, then say \emph{ailān} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{ऐलान} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An announcement\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{सावधान} (sāvdhān)}{सावधान (sāvdhān)}]{\hi{सावधान} (sāvdhān) — careful; on guard}

\label{lesson:HI-C302-savdhan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a warning, then the Hindi for an announcement.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{सावधान}}
\textbf{\hi{सावधान}} — \emph{sāvdhān} — \textquotedblleft{}careful; on guard\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{ऐलान} \hi{के} \hi{बाद} \hi{सब} \hi{लोग} \hi{सावधान} \hi{हो} \hi{गए।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ailān ke bād sab log sāvdhān ho gae.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
After the announcement everyone was on their guard.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{सावधान}} (\emph{sāvdhān}) is Sanskrit \emph{sāvadhāna}, \textquotedblleft{}attentive, heedful\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), taken over whole. Said alone on a sign it means \textquotedblleft{}Beware!\textquotedblright{}
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sāvdhān}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sāvdhān}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ailān ke bād sab log sāvdhān ho gae.} — After the announcement everyone was on their guard.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for a warning, then the Hindi for an announcement, then say \emph{sāvdhān} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{टलना} (ṭalnā)}{टलना (ṭalnā)}]{\hi{टलना} (ṭalnā) — to be averted; to be put off}

\label{lesson:HI-C302-ttalna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for an announcement, then the Hindi for careful.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{टलना}}
\textbf{\hi{टलना}} — \emph{ṭalnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to be averted; to be put off\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{सबकी} \hi{मदद} \hi{से} \hi{बड़ा} \hi{ख़तरा} \hi{टल} \hi{गया।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sabkī madad se baṛā khatrā ṭal gayā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
With everyone's help a great danger was averted.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \hi{वह} \hi{ख़तरा} \hi{टल} \hi{गया}, \emph{vah khatrā ṭal gayā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{टलना}} (\emph{ṭalnā}) is set by CDIAL under Sanskrit \emph{ṭalati}, \textquotedblleft{}moves aside\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 5450). A danger that \textbf{\hi{टल} \hi{गया}} moved away from you; a meeting that \textbf{\hi{टल} \hi{गई}} was put off.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭalnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭalnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sabkī madad se baṛā khatrā ṭal gayā.} — With everyone's help a great danger was averted.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for an announcement, then the Hindi for careful, then say \emph{ṭalnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
